correctness.rationale: On the dense kernel domain Fock analytic exponentials multiply and coanalytic exponentials translate, giving [T_{e^{az}},T_{overline{e^{bz}}}]u=(1-e^{a overline b})e^{az}u(z+overline b). After collecting repeated frequency pairs, coefficient q_ab=(1-e^{a overline b})(f_a overline g_b-h_a overline k_b). The normalized coherent-state diagonal equals finite exponential P(w)=sum q_ab exp(a w+overline b overline w). For bounded C, P is bounded: a generic exposed nonzero vertex of the convex hull of s=a+b gives positive exponential growth and a nonzero leading trigonometric sum with positive mean-square, so each off-anti-diagonal q vanishes. Remaining b=-a pieces equal e^{|a|²/2}q_a,-a W_overline a, a finite Weyl-unitary sum, proving sufficiency. Weyl displacements of fixed vectors weakly tend to 0 at infinity, while unitary conjugates of C have phase-subsequential norm limits; compact perturbations vanish on displaced vectors. Hence essential norm=ordinary norm, compact iff C=0. For <=2 Weyl frequencies factor one displacement and use full-circle spectrum of a nontrivial Weyl unitary to get exact sum of coefficient moduli, including example 2sinh(|a|²/2)+2sinh(|b|²/2). Independently checked 320 random complex test-kernel coefficient identities and Weyl normalization; these experiments do not establish the infinite-dimensional lemmas, which were reconstructed analytically.
